crime_highlights: The victim was held back by another individual while the appellant violently beat him and robbed him in his own home.
This left the victim with long lasting physical injuries and a feeling that he was no longer safe.
rationale_highlights: took into account the appellant’s Indigenous identity
obviously have to be factored into what ultimately is an appropriate sentence.
He explicitly stated that he would have sentenced the appellant to 15 to 18 months in custody rather than 12 months, were it not for the appellant’s Indigenous identity and personal history
note: Crime passage is short; only one paragraph describes the offence.

crime_highlights: Mr. Gray grabbed his chest and fell.
The appellant kind of “jumped over” them, chased Mr. Shakakeesic and fired two shots from just outside the front door.
the other struck the back of his upper left chest and shoulder, fatally injuring him.
He yelled out her name and said he was going to “blast” her “too”.
rationale_highlights: nowhere in his reasons did he analyze the effects of the systemic impact of colonization and intergenerational trauma experienced by the appellant on his moral blameworthiness for the offences
his life circumstances must be viewed as being, to a large extent, a manifestation of the effects of the systemic impacts of colonization and intergenerational trauma he experienced.
When viewed through that lens, his level of intoxication and state of agitation reduces his moral blameworthiness.

crime_highlights: on April 14, 2018, the appellant pushed her onto a bed and choked her
she took a selfie photograph showing a burst blood vessel in one of her eyes
a second photo showing marks on her neck
rationale_highlights: the Gladue and Morris factors in this case did not reduce the appellant’s moral culpability to such a degree to justify a sentence below the three-to-five-year range
the trial judge expressly recognized that the appellant was a victim of intergenerational trauma attributable to both his Indigenous and Black ancestry
the appellant’s Gladue and Morris factors, while mitigating, could only reduce the sentence so far
note: Court found factors mitigating but not enough to go below range.
